competencies.text: Identify how physics concepts improve quality of life in household, health & safety, work productivity, and leisure.

days.title: Introduction to Physics in Daily Life
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to explain how physics concepts improve the quality of life in four key areas: household, health & safety, work productivity, and leisure.

🔍 What Is Physics?

Physics is the branch of science that studies matter, energy, motion, force, light, sound, heat, and electricity. It explains why things work the way they do — from why a ball rolls downhill to how your phone's screen displays images.

Physics is not just formulas in a textbook. It is everywhere in your daily life:

AreaPhysics in ActionExample in Your Life
🏠 HouseholdHeat, electricity, pressureRice cooker, electric fan, water pump, refrigerator
🏥 Health & SafetyOptics, radiation, forcesX-ray machines, eyeglasses, seatbelts, helmets
💼 Work ProductivityMachines, electricity, torqueWheelbarrow, sewing machine, welding equipment, computers
🎮 LeisureWaves, optics, motionTelevisions, speakers, sports, video games, cameras

⚙️ The Four Core Physics Concepts You'll Meet

  1. Motion & Forces — how and why objects move (Newton's Laws).
  2. Energy & Work — how energy changes from one form to another (Law of Conservation of Energy).
  3. Waves & Light — how energy travels through space (sound, light, radio).
  4. Electricity & Magnetism — how charged particles create current and fields.

💡 Key Idea

Every time you use a tool, ride a vehicle, turn on a light, or hear a sound — physics is making it possible. Understanding physics helps you use technology safely, make informed choices, and even invent new solutions to everyday problems.

📌 Quick Check

  • Name one household appliance that uses electricity.
  • Name one sports activity that depends on motion and forces.
  • Why is a helmet important? What physics principle protects your head?

days.title: Match Game — Physics Applications
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

In this activity, match each physics concept to the correct everyday application. There are 8 pairs. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

Tip: Read both columns carefully. Think about what physics is doing in each situation.

match.right: A straw appearing bent in water
Hearing a person speak on the phone
Using a long wrench to loosen a bolt

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Life Areas
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best physics-based reasoning for the situation. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🏠 Your mother complains that the electric fan is not cooling the room enough on a hot day. Which physics concept best explains why an electric fan does NOT actually cool the air?

choices.label: A) The fan creates cold air from electricity.
B) The fan moves air, which increases evaporation from the skin, making you feel cooler — but the air temperature stays the same.
C) The fan absorbs heat from the room.
D) The fan uses gravity to push hot air outside.

scenario.text: 🏥 A nurse checks your blood pressure using a cuff and a pressure gauge. What physics principle does this device rely on?

choices.label: B) Fluid pressure and force transmission

scenario.text: 💼 A carpenter uses a long crowbar to pull out a stubborn nail. Why does a longer crowbar work better than a shorter one?

choices.label: B) It increases the torque by increasing the lever arm distance.

scenario.text: 🎮 You are watching a live basketball game on TV. Which type of wave carries the video signal to your television?
🚗 You are riding a jeepney and the driver suddenly brakes. You feel pushed forward. Which physics principle explains this?

choices.label: A) Newton's First Law of Motion (inertia)
B) Newton's Third Law of Motion
D) Law of Conservation of Energy

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. Answer each question correctly to earn a key. Wrong answers cost one life. You need 75% (5 of 6) to escape and complete this week.

Think carefully! Once you lose all 3 lives, you must retake.

escape.text: Which area of daily life is MOST directly improved by understanding friction?

choices.label: B) Walking on a wet floor without slipping

escape.text: Which physics concept explains why X-ray images can pass through your skin but not your bones?
A construction worker wears a safety helmet. Which physics principle is the helmet designed to address?

choices.label: A) Reducing impact force by extending collision time

escape.text: You use a wheelbarrow to carry soil. Which simple machine does this represent, and what is its main advantage?

choices.label: A) Pulley — changes direction of force
B) Lever — multiplies force to lift heavy loads with less effort
C) Inclined plane — reduces effort by spreading distance

escape.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of physics improving work productivity?

choices.label: A) A sewing machine speeding up garment production
B) A welding machine joining metal parts
C) A worker taking a nap during break time
D) A computer processing documents instantly

escape.text: You are watching a friend play a guitar. Which type of wave produces the sound you hear?
